title: Amazon Product Photos on White and in Use | AIVideosUGC
description: Make Amazon product photos from pictures you already have: clean white-background main images plus lifestyle and detail shots for your gallery. Try it now.
h1: Amazon Product Photos for Your Main Image and Listing Gallery
lead: Amazon product photos start with a clean white main image, then add photos that show size, detail and real use, so shoppers can judge the product without holding it.
card: A clean white main image, then photos for size, detail and use.
intro: On Amazon, your photos do the work a store shelf would do. The main image has to be clean and plain so it looks right in search results, and the rest of the gallery has to answer what a shopper would ask in person: How big is it? What's in the box? What does it look like on a counter? AIVideosUGC turns the product photos you already have into new square images, from a white-background main shot to lifestyle and close-up scenes.

It's made for sellers who need a fuller gallery without reshooting every item. Upload a phone photo of your product, pick a white background or describe a setting, and download the result. For front, side and back views, photograph each side and use the Every Angle template to keep the gallery consistent. You can also make a short 16:9 or 1:1 video if your listing has room for one. Callouts and text labels go on afterward in Canva or another design tool.
tips: Use a pure white background for the main image, and check Amazon's current rules for your category before uploading, since requirements vary by category.
Keep the main image free of added text, badges and props; save those for the other gallery slots.
Fill the rest of the gallery with a scale shot, a close-up of the materials and a photo of the item in use.

ideas.d: Turn a photo taken on your kitchen table into a square shot on plain white for the first image slot.
Place a wallet beside a phone or a planter beside a coffee mug so shoppers can judge the size at a glance.

ideas.t: Lifestyle shot in the right room
ideas.d: Show a cutting board on a counter with chopped vegetables, or a bath mat in a bright bathroom.

faq.q: Does this work for Amazon main images?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your product photo and choose a white background to get a square image of the item on plain white. Look it over closely before you upload, as you would with any photo.

faq.q: Can I add text callouts to my gallery images?
faq.a: Add them yourself in Canva or a similar design app. Letters drawn by AI can come out wrong, and a separate text layer is easier to correct later.

faq.q: Can I make a video for my Amazon listing?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a 16:9 or 1:1 shape and 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds of run time, then download the file and add it to your listing from your seller account.
Amazon requires a realistic product on pure white, with the item filling at least 85% of the frame. The image must be 500–10,000 pixels on the longest side; 1,000+ enables zoom.

overview.h2: Treat the main image as a proof of the item
overview.d: Amazon shoppers meet the product first in the main image. Start with a photo that shows the complete item, then use a pure white background and a centered composition with no extra words, badges, or props. Amazon's current guide says the product should fill at least 85% of the frame, the longest side should be 500–10,000 pixels, and 1,000 or more pixels enables zoom. Compare the downloaded result with the live requirement for your category before uploading.

overview.h2: Use the gallery to answer the next questions
overview.d: Secondary images can show a close-up, a scale comparison, the parts in the box, and the product in a room. Build each view from a source photo that actually shows the relevant side or component. AIVideosUGC currently returns square stills by default and can make 6, 10, 15, or 30 second clips in 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4 when your listing supports video; the cost appears before each job.

input_guide.h2: Prepare a source for a trustworthy listing

items.d: Keep every part that ships with the product inside the frame. Do not expect a hidden side, cable, or accessory to appear accurately later.
For the main-image starting point, face the product toward the camera and keep the lens level so its proportions are easier to compare.
Take additional photos of the sole, clasp, ports, texture, or inside compartment when a shopper needs that information.

results.h2: A gallery with a job for every frame

items.d: A pure-white product view that follows the current Amazon category rules and leaves out promotional text.
A close view of the material, mechanism, finish, or label that cannot be judged from the first shot.
A scene with a familiar object or a clearly stated real dimension added by you, so shoppers are not asked to guess.

scene_recipes.h2: Gallery scenes that answer shopper questions

items.d: Place a cutting board beside a mixing bowl on a kitchen counter, with a familiar mug nearby for context and no invented measurements.
Show a backpack standing upright with its main compartment open and the zipper, lining, and pockets visible.
Lay a watch or bag on a plain surface with the clasp, buckle, or stitching close enough to inspect.
Put a bath mat in front of a real-looking tub or a lamp on a side table, keeping the product's edges clear.

after_download.h2: Review every file before Seller Central

items.d: Check shape, color, parts, finish, and label against the physical product before you upload the asset.
Verify the pure-white background, product coverage, and pixel dimensions against Amazon's current category guidance.
Type dimensions, material names, prices, and feature labels yourself on secondary images, where the wording can be checked.
Remove props, added text, badges, and watermarks from the main image when the current rules require a clean product view.

fit.h2: Useful for an Amazon image set
good: Physical products with a clear, complete source photo
Listings that need a white main image plus detail and lifestyle frames
Sellers willing to verify the current category rules before upload
Products whose dimensions and claims can be added accurately after download
not_ideal: Items whose critical features are absent from every source photo
Claims that depend on an AI-generated label or measurement being exact
